payload.problem_agreed:
KILLER. Unchanged in substance and now carrying its own proof.

MEASURED: 4131 calls; se_file_patch most-used (645) and most-failing (28) at one edit per call; six se_help misses across three days on the one capability never served; a porting law mandating two sources the lane could not open.

THE REWALK'S FINDING: se.meth-gate-review has required verify/validate/redteam/verdict since it was written; no evidence form collected them; NOT ONE was ever filled, in any gate, in any iteration. The note predicted its own fix - 'the compiler will inject the standard fields; until then, fill them from here' - and nothing did.

THE PROOF THAT THIS IS SYSTEMIC RATHER THAN CARELESSNESS, and it is the strongest evidence in this gate: I BUILT the injection, wrote a guard for it, and then TWO GATES LATER filled gate_inputs without the rounds and had to dismiss my own offer. Knowing the rule, having just implemented it, caring about it - and the form did not ask, so I did not do it. That is a controlled experiment with n=1 and me as the subject.

THE COST: R3 was written, violated by the design claiming to satisfy it, defended by an ADR, and passed green - caught by the owner reading, not by the machine.

payload.redteam_round:
THE OPPOSING CASE, STEELMANNED IN INCREASING STRICTNESS. Five attacks, each stronger than the last, each stated at its best before I answer.

KILL-CRITERION, named first: THIS GATE SHOULD FAIL IF THE MOTIVATION IS PROCEDURAL RATHER THAN REAL — if the honest diagnosis is 'the agent was careless' or if the proposed fix cannot work. Attacks 4 and 5 below go directly at that.

ATTACK 1 (mildest) — YAK-SHAVING. 'A full day on tools and process while the product stands still.' STEELMANNED: the owner has a mechatronics career and finite evenings; every hour on the machine is an hour not spent on what the machine is for. ANSWER: the measured tax is real (645 calls through a one-edit-per-call tool, three workarounds in a day, three owner rounds re-deriving rulings the design doc already contained) and it compounds across every future iteration. WEAKEST attack; does not approach the kill-criterion.

ATTACK 2 — NEGLIGENCE DRESSED AS SYSTEM DEFECT. 'The rounds were documented. You read the guidance at write_requirements that names the scan in plain words. Nothing stopped you. You are proposing machinery to compensate for not reading.' STEELMANNED: partly TRUE and I concede it — I read that guidance and did not perform the scan; attention failed, not the system alone. ANSWER: the same failure appears across three independent mechanisms, two iterations, and every gate in the project's history including ones walked in earlier sessions by earlier context. A failure with that distribution is not a person. And the decisive datum is the one I generated by accident: having JUST built the injection and written its guard, I filled the next gate without the rounds. That is negligence AND system, and the system half is the half you can fix.

ATTACK 3 — THE FIX IS THEATRE. 'You made the reviewer the same entity as the author. v1 had a human. You have an agent writing a critique of its own work and grading it. Four required fields cannot manufacture adversarial intent.' STEELMANNED: this is strong, and it is the attack I cannot fully defeat. A required field can always be satisfied with well-written agreement, and I am the one judging whether my own red-team was adversarial enough. ANSWER, partial: the kill-criterion converts a vibe into a commitment made BEFORE the outcome is known — naming what would falsify me, then reporting what I found, is checkable by a reader even if my sincerity is not. And this very round is producing findings that hurt (R3 still violated in code; the tool that cannot reach a live session). But I record this as UNRESOLVED, not answered: se.raid-mandatory-rounds-degrade-into-ceremony exists precisely because attack 3 lands.

ATTACK 4 — CIRCULARITY, and this one aims at the kill-criterion. 'You changed the machine mid-iteration, landed it on trunk out of band, and are now using the changed machine to bless the iteration that changed it. The gate that validates the injection is a gate that only exists in its injected form BECAUSE of the injection. That is not a review; it is a system certifying itself.' STEELMANNED at full strength: this is structurally identical to a compiler being tested only by code it compiled. ANSWER: the circularity is REAL and it is bounded rather than vicious. What the injection is being credited with is not 'it made me conclude the right thing' but a MECHANICAL fact independently checkable by anyone: the four fields are present and required on every gate, asserted by a test that does not involve my judgement (4/4, and re-run in trunk before commit). The JUDGEMENT this gate exercises is the same judgement it would have exercised uninjected — the form changes what is ASKED, not what is true. And the failure it claims to fix was demonstrated BEFORE the fix existed, twice. What would make this vicious: if the injection's value rested on my saying the rounds helped. It does not; it rests on next iteration's measurable counts, which is why those are the signals.

ATTACK 5 (strictest) — G5 IS UNFALSIFIABLE, SO BLESSING ON IT IS FAITH. 'You ranked G5 above G2 — prose above computation — on the claim that a round catches what a lint cannot. You have exactly one datum: the owner caught R3 by reading. That proves a HUMAN reading catches it. It does not prove an AGENT reading catches it, and the agent already failed to catch it once. You are ranking your own future diligence first, and you cannot know whether it works until an iteration you also run.' STEELMANNED: this is the strongest attack and it goes straight at the kill-criterion, because if true, the motivation reduces to 'I will try harder, but with fields'. I LOOKED FOR IT HONESTLY. What I found cuts both ways. AGAINST me: yes, the agent-reading-the-register case is unproven, and the one time it mattered the agent missed it. FOR the gate: in THIS round, agent-reading-the-register just produced two findings that cost me — R3 still violated in the shipped code, and tools not reaching live sessions — neither of which any lint we could build would catch, and both of which I would rather not have had to write. That is weak evidence (n=1, and I am the subject again) but it is evidence in the direction the claim needs. VERDICT ON ATTACK 5: it does not kill the gate, but it CHANGES what this gate may claim. G5's ranking above G2 is now recorded as a HYPOTHESIS UNDER TEST rather than a settled ruling, with its falsifier named: if the next iteration's retro finds no round changed any conclusion, G5 drops below G2 and the answer becomes an adversarial second party rather than better prose.

NO OVERRIDE IS TAKEN. Every acceptance item is met on its own terms. Attack 3 remains unresolved and is logged rather than answered; attack 5 forced a real change to what the gate asserts.
payload.verdict:
PASS.

All five acceptance items met. Three rounds ran and each changed something: VERIFY found N2's pass line was the hole rather than the design alone; VALIDATE found R3 still violated in code that has now shipped to trunk, plus a fifth built-but-not-reaching instance (a new tool cannot be called in a live session); RED-TEAM's fifth attack forced G5's priority to be restated as a HYPOTHESIS UNDER TEST with a named falsifier, rather than a settled ruling.

NOT A CLEAN PASS, and the outstanding items are named rather than deferred silently:
- R3 IS VIOLATED IN LIVE CODE ON TRUNK. It must be fixed before gate_architecture, and gate_architecture is where a reopen verdict belongs if it is not.
- se.adr-locate-and-read-are-separate must be retired and se.adr-git-is-the-only-searcher superseded, per the owner's correction that tree-search and record-search are two jobs.
- Attack 3 (the reviewer is the author) is unresolved by construction and carried as a risk, not as a finding.

No states reopened by this verdict. The next gate inherits the R3 obligation as a blocking item.
